descriptionChirho: The result or content of deliberation: a resolved plan, purpose, or intention, whether divine or human. Cognate noun of βουλεύω (to deliberate). Cross-linguistically stable: Arabic مشورة/مقاصد (counsel/purposes), German Rat/Ratschluss (counsel/decree), Spanish consejo/voluntad/resolucion, Hebrew עצה (counsel), Korean 뜻/계획 (will/plan), Hindi योजना/इच्छा (plan/desire), French conseil. Predominantly used of God's sovereign plan: Acts 2:23 (delivered by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God), Acts 4:28 (what God's hand and counsel predetermined), Acts 13:36 (David served God's counsel in his own generation), Acts 20:27 (the whole counsel of God), Eph 1:11 (the counsel of His will), Heb 6:17 (the unchangeableness of God's purpose). Also used of human decisions: Luke 7:30 (Pharisees rejected God's counsel for themselves), Luke 23:51 (Joseph had not consented to their plan and action), Acts 27:12,42 (the majority's plan regarding the voyage). 1 Cor 4:5 (the counsels/intentions of the hearts revealed at judgment). All singular, plural, and case forms represent one semantic core of deliberated purpose.
